sources.name: Austin Water rainwater harvesting rebate
sources.summary: Austin Water lists a rainwater harvesting rebate of up to $5,000, based on system capacity.
sources.eligibility: Austin Water customers; confirm the current account and project requirements before buying equipment.
sources.application_requirements: Use the City of Austin Conservation Hub and confirm whether pre-approval is required.
sources.funding_status: Subject to current program rules and funding availability.

sources.name: Texas Water Development Board rainwater harvesting guidance
sources.summary: The Texas Water Development Board explains statewide tax and property-law provisions and publishes rainwater harvesting guidance.
sources.eligibility: Statewide guidance; local plumbing, health, and building rules may add requirements.
sources.application_requirements: Consult local authorities for permits and treatment requirements.
sources.funding_status: Guidance resource, not a rebate promise.

sources.name: SoCal Water$mart rain barrel and cistern rebates
sources.summary: SoCal Water$mart lists rain barrel and cistern rebates for customers of participating water agencies.
sources.eligibility: Customers of participating Southern California water agencies; rebate amounts vary by agency.
sources.application_requirements: Check the current program page and agency-specific terms before purchase.
sources.funding_status: Funding and available amounts vary by water agency and may change.

sources.name: Ley 91-2024: Ley para la Recolección y Cosecha de Agua de Lluvia en Puerto Rico
sources.summary: Ley 91-2024 (June 4, 2024) establishes public policy to promote rainwater harvesting and directs government agencies to take steps including education, projects in government buildings, regulations, and feasibility studies.
sources.eligibility: The act establishes policy and agency duties; it does not describe a residential rebate or certified community program.
sources.application_requirements: The act does not specify a residential application process or general residential permit exemption.
sources.funding_status: No household rebate or grant is established by this act.

sources.name: Tucson Water Rainwater Harvesting Rebate
sources.summary: Tucson Water offers a rainwater harvesting rebate of up to $1,999 per property under its July 2026 policy updates: up to $1,900 for qualifying catchment storage ($1.00/gallon for direct systems sized to capture at least 1 inch of roof rainfall; $0.50/gallon for undersized direct or indirect passive systems) plus an optional Treebate of up to $99 for planting 1–2 qualifying drought-tolerant trees ($50 for the first tree, $49 for the second).
sources.eligibility: Tucson Water single-family residential customers or small commercial customers (5/8-inch water meter) with active Tucson Water service prior to purchasing and installing the system. Harvested water must meet Tucson Water's Beneficial Use policy; optional Treebates apply only to new drought-tolerant trees on the TAMA Low Water Use Plant List watered by the rebated system.
sources.application_requirements: Complete the required Watershed Management Group workshop (taken after July 2023), submit before photos and a labeled site plan showing roof area, storage capacity, flow arrows, and beneficial uses, and review Tucson Water's current application form and design standards before installing.
sources.funding_status: Application form reopened in July 2026 under updated One Water 2100 Plan rules. Rebate funding is limited; submitting a form does not guarantee funding, and Tucson Water may change or cancel the program without prior notice.
